periods.public: The group discusses which metrics are most critical for evaluating the proposals. They weigh the importance of financial constraints, operational inefficiencies, and historical success rates.

lines.Daisuke: Suggests looking at daily losses and incident logs.
lines.May: Suggests checking staff availability and coordination group staffing.
lines.Shunichi: Suggests checking network coverage and vendor pricing.
lines.Ryuji: Suggests checking the capital budget and software allowance.
lines.Kenji: Suggests checking previous rollout outcomes and standardization efforts.

lines.Daisuke: Agrees with Kenji on the value of historical records.
lines.May: Questions if the budget is actually flexible.
lines.Shunichi: Points out that external dependencies are often ignored.
lines.Ryuji: Emphasizes the need to know where the money comes from.
lines.Kenji: Wants to see if the same mistakes are being repeated.

lines.Daisuke: Adds that copying records is a hidden time sink.
lines.May: Asks about the burden on the coordination group.
lines.Shunichi: Mentions the risk of vendor license costs.
lines.Ryuji: Asks about the software allowance specifically.
lines.Kenji: Suggests looking at the record of standardization.

periods.public: Participants share the findings from their research. They debate the feasibility of projects based on budget freezes, staffing shortages, and technical limitations at customer sites.

lines.Daisuke: Reports on time lost to copying and misrouted deliveries.
lines.May: Reports on the lack of staffing in the coordination group.
lines.Shunichi: Reports on poor network coverage and visitor approval delays.
lines.Ryuji: Reports on the frozen capital line and available software allowance.
lines.Kenji: Reports that narrow tools survived while broad ones failed.

lines.Daisuke: Notes that the delivery errors are not due to inexperience.
lines.May: Highlights that two people are doing all the manual logging.
lines.Shunichi: Warns that some sites lose signal for whole afternoons.
lines.Ryuji: Clarifies that only recurring software funds are available.
lines.Kenji: Mentions that standardization efforts often end without owners.

lines.Daisuke: Asks if any proposal addresses the copying issue.
lines.May: Questions who will actually manage the new tools.
lines.Shunichi: Asks if any proposal relies on external site access.
lines.Ryuji: Warns against projects requiring capital expenditure.
lines.Kenji: Suggests avoiding tools that require daily entry from everyone.

periods.public: The group evaluates the four candidates against the discovered constraints. They compare the risk of failure against the potential for solving daily operational pains.

lines.Daisuke: Argues that one candidate solves the copying and delivery issues.
lines.May: Considers if that candidate adds too much work to the staff.
lines.Shunichi: Notes that one candidate is impossible due to network issues.
lines.Ryuji: Checks which candidates fit the software allowance budget.
lines.Kenji: Points out which candidate avoids the 'daily entry' trap.

lines.Daisuke: Points out the efficiency gain of a central repository.
lines.May: Agrees if the update procedure is shared and not centralized.
lines.Shunichi: Notes that a central hub doesn't depend on plant signal.
lines.Ryuji: Confirms a hub fits the recurring software budget.
lines.Kenji: Observes that a catalog is a narrow, sustainable tool.

lines.Daisuke: Asks for a final consensus on the hub.
lines.May: Agrees it is the most realistic option for the staff.
lines.Shunichi: Agrees it avoids the technical pitfalls mentioned.
lines.Ryuji: Agrees it is the only financially viable path.
lines.Kenji: Agrees it aligns with the patterns of past success.

seats.Ryuji: Focuses on the source of funding and long-term costs. He evaluates candidates based on their alignment with the available budget lines.
seats.Shunichi: Concerned with external dependencies and technical prerequisites. He analyzes candidates by looking for risks related to site access and vendor pricing.
seats.Kenji: Interested in the longevity and survival rate of previous projects. He looks for candidates that avoid the pitfalls of past failures.
seats.Daisuke: Prioritizes the reduction of daily operational friction and errors. He advocates for candidates that address documented workplace inefficiencies.
seats.May: Worried about the impact on human resources and staff burnout. She examines candidates based on the additional workload they impose on employees.
